question: Do the public terms of use or API terms of Daffy, Endaoment, Every.org and Chariot allow a donor to store an API key or OAuth grant with a third-party tool router (Composio, Pipedream, Zapier), and who is liable for a donation or gift such a wrapper initiates? Read the published terms, API terms and privacy policies (no login) and record clauses on credential sharing, agent use, unauthorised transactions and refunds
conclusion_affected: F16 credential-compromise exposure; sponsor control over agent-originated recommendations
rationale: Five third-party wrappers expose Daffy write actions (Composio Create Gift; Pipedream Create Donation plus a proxy to any endpoint; Zapier Create Donation and Create Gift; Metorial; Operator.io re-wrapping Composio and Pipedream). Daffy keys have no documented scopes, and Daffy's MCP and auth pages do not mention any wrapper except the Zapier one its staff built. Whether sponsor terms forbid or allocate liability for key sharing is unknown

question: When Every.org's first Form 990 (CY2025) and FY2024 audited statements appear, re-run the recipient analysis: share of grants paid to Network for Good (ForGood rail), PayPal Giving Fund, 'Hyperwallet activity' and named charities. Also confirm what the CY2023 'HYPERWALLET ACTIVITY' line ($283,570) records
conclusion_affected: Every.org rail mix; nonprofit receipt cost by rail
rationale: CY2020-2024 990-PF Part XV shows the ForGood rail (Network for Good, a single recipient always above the itemisation threshold) falling from 73.9% to 1.1% of grants. Stripe Connect and PayPal Grants both pay the charity directly, so they cannot be split from the return. Hyperwallet is a PayPal payout service; its 2023 line is the only PayPal-family signal besides a $6,201 PPGF grant

question: Build a dated panel of published electronic-vs-check shares for DAF grant payments, 2023-2026, by sponsor and rail: Chariot ('94.57% sent electronically since launch'), Fidelity Charitable (67% of 3m grants electronic in 2025, per Chariot; electronic-only from July 2026), DJCF 92%, Founders Pledge 98%, Charityvest (95% of checks deposited within 35 days), NPT and Vanguard PayPal volumes. Confirm each figure on the sponsor's own page
conclusion_affected: Paper-check persistence; whether electronic rails remove checks
rationale: No sponsor or PayPal publishes a PayPal Grant Payments expiry rate. Chariot's aggregate implies about 5.4% of its grant payments went by check since launch, but it is a vendor figure with no sponsor split. Fidelity's 67% comes second-hand from Chariot
